summary: Mars never visibly hits his gut; it flies up and out of frame and he is hit by a flash cut, with a hard white flash and a jump to a different scene at the end.

faults.what: Mars is a huge sphere that swings across his head and shoulder. His head and the dark hair clip into and through the planet, and the planet surface shows a black tear or gap as it passes (115.99-116.13).
faults.fix: Fix the planet's path so it clears his head, and remove the dark cutout or mesh hole on its surface.

faults.what: Mars jumps in scale and position between tiles. It is cut off at the top at 116.06-116.09, then sits behind his head at 116.13 and beside his torso at 116.16, so it reads as a teleport rather than a continuous arc. His torso also bends sharply at 116.06, and his arm and head snap.
faults.fix: Key the planet on a smooth arc with consistent scale, and ease his duck pose.

faults.what: The beat is meant to be 'he ducks Saturn', but Saturn is only a tiny dot that grows slowly. Mars exits upward and he stands upright and unaffected. Nothing reads as dodging.
faults.fix: Add a clear duck pose and have Saturn pass close to him.

faults.what: Two frames at 118.23 and 118.26 wash out to flat grey and then snap back to the dark scene at 118.29. This is a full-frame flash that reads as a glitch, not an impact. Mars is a tiny planet and far from his gut, so the 'gut' hit is not shown.
faults.fix: Shorten the flash to one frame with a bright white colour, and move Mars into his midsection on the impact frame.

faults.what: The last frame cuts to a different scene with a different character, in blue, and an Earth, with fragments and rings. It breaks continuity with the red-shirt character and the setup, and Mars never lands.
faults.fix: Show the impact on him in this shot before the cut, or keep the cut clean.
